title: A word that never existed sat in Webster’s dictionary for years
body: In 1931 a chemistry editor at the Merriam company filed a slip reading ‘D or d, cont./density’, meaning the letter D can abbreviate density. It was misread as one word, and the 1934 Webster’s New International Dictionary defined ‘dord’ as a term for density in physics and chemistry. An editor noticed in 1939 that it had no etymology, but the ghost word was not fully removed until 1947.
